findings.summary: Turning every non-alphanumeric run into a space breaks each path into several words, so a criterion naming a long path falls outside the 8-word window and is missed.
findings.evidence: Normalised, 'No file outside crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs is changed' becomes 'no file outside crates athena core src run pin tests rs is changed'. 'changed' is the 10th word after 'outside', beyond the 8-word window of form (a), so the job is left unchecked. The request's own example is 'no file outside X changed', and in real use X is usually a path. Shorter real cases, such as structure-pass.md:229 'No file outside the gh/ or run/ directory changes', still fit. Fix: Split on whitespace only, trimming punctuation at the ends of each token, so a path counts as one word, or count any token containing '/' or '.' as one word. Add a positive unit test with a path of five or more segments.

findings.summary: The fixed paragraph of the existing send-back says 'This is the only send-back' and that remaining work goes to the verifier. Both are false for a scoped send-back, and the new section says the opposite.
findings.evidence: send_back.rs:142-145: 'This is the only send-back: if your changes are still in place afterwards, they go to the verifier...'. Under decision 7 a scoped job can be sent back twice, and the new section says a file still outside closes the job before the verifier runs. Keeping the None case byte-identical is right, but the scoped text gives the producer contradictory instructions. Fix: In the scoped section's leading sentence, say that for files outside the allowed paths, this sentence overrides the 'only send-back' and 'go to the verifier' wording below. Assert that sentence in the send_back_text_scoped test.

findings.summary: A retry reads the request again, so its reading can add a limit the first run never had. A Verifier-stage resume then skips the scope check, although the plan says such a resume 'passed on its first run'.
findings.evidence: run/mod.rs:645 sets recorded_checks only for ResumeStage::Verifier with matching checks, and mod.rs:1075 resumes after the retry's own Job record, with a new allowed_paths, has been written. The decision gate's guard is sound because decisions do not depend on the reading. The scope limit does. Fix: Run the scope gate whenever a list is stored and the run is not nested, without the recorded_checks guard. The check is path-only and costs nothing. If the guard stays, state this case in the doc comment.

findings.summary: When the plan lists a file that is not a deliverable, one scoped send-back both asks for it to be changed and asks for it to be reverted.
findings.evidence: planned_paths uses the plan's files as well as the deliverables. This plan shows the case itself: producer.rs, store.rs and docs/records.md are planned but are not deliverables. Under a limiting reading, unchanged_planned_files demands those files when they are left unchanged, while the scope section demands their revert when they are changed. Fix: For a job with a stored list, drop paths outside the list from the 'Planned files left unchanged' list, or say in the scoped text that the allowed paths win. Add a pure test for it.

findings.summary: The scoped wrapper is described as changing only acceptance_criteria. The only fake deliverable is README.md, which the counting producer also edits, so there is no separate allowed file to delete.
findings.evidence: run/tests.rs:233: "deliverables": [{ "path": "README.md", ... }]. editing() at 2234 adds extra edits to the README edit. An allowed deletion needs a second deliverable, or a README.md deletion that does not conflict with the counting edit. Fix: Let the wrapper also add a deliverable (for example a seeded file with action delete) for the deletion test, or say that the pure test alone covers in-list deletion.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 2 (end-to-end deletion of an allowed file) / step 9 wrapper

findings.summary: governed_job is the helper for the decision-gate tests. If its repository's decisions govern any of the edited files, the gate could close the 'unaffected' job before the verifier, and the 1-verifier assertion would fail for an unrelated reason.
findings.evidence: run/tests.rs:2252-2284 runs over a repository passed in by the caller. The gate tests at 2303-2480 use the same helper with a governed repository. Fix: Use an ungoverned repository, or say which repository the unscoped test uses.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 3 (unscoped end-to-end test via governed_job)

summary: I checked the round-3 plan against the snapshot using Read and Grep; I ran nothing. The code it names exists where it says. producer_loop is at run/producer.rs:162, with the change list at 268, the decision gate at 279, the break condition at 290, report_problems at 315, the limit test at 336 and the text built at 359-365. check_and_verify is at run/mod.rs:1544, with the decision gate at 1565 and push_ci_branch at 1583. The Job literal is at mod.rs:994, and `accepted` is in scope from line 944. resume_candidate is called at line 1075, after the Job is recorded. recorded_checks is set only for a Verifier-stage resume (line 645). retry_findings filters on GATE_REASON_PREFIX at reading.rs:1799. The plan lists every Job literal I found: mod.rs, store.rs:650, reading.rs:5735 and 6036, and records.rs:5074. The JSON fixtures in pr_check.rs and landing_tests.rs have no new key, so they still parse. The fake reader at run/tests.rs:233 declares README.md as a deliverable, so a scoped wrapper does get a non-empty list. The design follows the accepted reading: the list comes from the deliverables, it is stored on Job with the same serde attributes as dispatch_branch, a check runs at two points, and the extra send-back is put to the user as an open question. The demonstrations name real seams, and each would fail without the behavior. Parsing criterion text for phrases is a heuristic, but the user accepted it in the reading, and the plan narrows it with windows and negative tests. What remains is minor. The windows count path segments as words, so a criterion naming a long path can be missed. The existing send-back text contradicts the scoped section. A Verifier-stage resume under a newly limiting reading skips the check. A planned file outside the list gets two opposite instructions in one send-back. The end-to-end deletion test needs the wrapper to add a deliverable as well as a criterion.
